episodes.180932: An upper level disturbance passing over CO combined with sufficient low-level moisture allowed for scattered storms to develop over northeastern NM during the afternoon of July 19th. These scattered storms stayed over very rural areas through the mid-to-late afternoon period likely producing strong winds and large hail. There was only one report of an estimated severe wind gust just east of Gladstone, NM however.
episodes.180961: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms moved across central Indiana yesterday which generally remained sub-severe outside of a lone stronger storm near Lafayette where several large tree limbs were downed.
episodes.180974: A combination of squall line thunderstorms tied to a strong cold front and pre-frontal supercells brought severe weather to parts of Southeast Michigan Thursday afternoon and early evening on July 20,2023. One supercell that developed just before the arrival of the squall line produced 2.75 inch (Baseball size) hail over Davison, MI leading to widespread hail damage to vehicles, homes, and businesses.  Several other locations also received severe hail, including Ypsilanti where 2 inch (Lime size) hail fell and Ann Arbor which experienced 1.5 inch (Ping Pong size) hail, shutting down the Ann Arbor Art Fair for a couple hours. Additionally, there were numerous reports of downed trees (some of which fell on homes), several measured wind gusts in excess of 50 mph, and a waterspout over Anchor Bay. DTE reported 90,000 residents without power due to downed power lines.  The outages were mainly along and south of I-69 to the I-94 corridor.
episodes.181003: A line of severe thunderstorms, aided by some upper energy and deep layer shear, developed over north Georgia and moved SE across the Central Savannah River Area of GA, during the late day and evening, and produced widespread wind damage.
episodes.181004: A line of severe thunderstorms, aided by some upper energy and deep layer shear, developed over north Georgia and moved SE across the Midlands of SC, during the late day and evening, and produced widespread wind damage.  Ahead of this line, isolated thunderstorms, one severe, developed earlier in the afternoon.
episodes.181341: A very strong squall line made its way through Middle Tennessee during the morning and afternoon hours of July 20, 2023. Damaging straight-line winds were the primary threat associated with this line of thunderstorms with wind gusts of 65 to 80 mph common. The most significant damage was reported in Sumner and Wilson counties with numerous reports of downed trees and powerlines received. Meanwhile, training showers and thunderstorms preceding this line across the Cumberland Plateau produced heavy rainfall in this area, particularly in Fentress County. Five to eight inches of rainfall in total resulted in significant flash flooding.
episodes.181405: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved into the Nebraska Panhandle from eastern Wyoming late in the afternoon on the 19th producing large hail in southern Sioux County.
episodes.181439: A thunderstorm complex moved east-southeast across southern Illinois. A thunderstorm along the leading edge of this complex produced damaging winds in Massac County. The storms occurred along and ahead of a cold front that stretched from the Great Lakes region to the southern Plains.
episodes.181440: A thunderstorm cluster moved east-southeast across Cape Girardeau County. The lead thunderstorm contained locally strong winds. The storms occurred along and ahead of a cold front that stretched from the Great Lakes region to the southern Plains.
episodes.181441: A thunderstorm complex moved east-southeast across western Kentucky. A thunderstorm along the leading edge of this complex produced locally damaging winds from the Paducah area eastward to the northern part of the Land-Between-The-Lakes region. The storms occurred along and ahead of a cold front that stretched from the Great Lakes region to the southern Plains.
episodes.181590: Widely scattered showers and storms formed over south-central Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of July 19, 2023 in a moderately unstable (MLCAPE 1500 J/Kg) environment ahead of an approaching shortwave. Once storm became strong enough to produce wind damage in York County.
episodes.181591: A squall line pushed from the Great Lakes into central Pennsylvania during the evening of July 20, 2023. An intense storm formed just ahead of the squall line over Warren County producing damaging winds and large hail. Then the squall line arrived with more widespread damaging winds as it crossed central Pennsylvania from northwest to southeast through the late evening and early overnight hours.
episodes.181606: Thunderstorms that formed over the central Great Lakes during the morning survived and tracked east across western New York by early evening. The most instability was built up just southwest of the region across Ohio and western Pennsylvania which resulted in the most concentrated wind damage occurring over Chautauqua County, while wind damage was more sporadic farther north across western New York. A storm survey was conducted in the following days near Lake Erie State Park in western Chautauqua County, but the damage observed was concluded to be caused by straight line winds.
episodes.181607: Thunderstorms that formed over the central Great Lakes during the morning survived and tracked east across western New York by early evening. The most instability was built up just southwest of the region across Ohio and western Pennsylvania which resulted in the most concentrated wind damage occurring over Chautauqua County, while wind damage was more sporadic farther north across western New York. A storm survey was conducted in the following days near Lake Erie State Park in western Chautauqua County, but the damage observed was concluded to be caused by straight line winds.
episodes.181608: Thunderstorms that formed over the central Great Lakes during the morning survived and tracked east across western New York by early evening. The most instability was built up just southwest of the region across Ohio and western Pennsylvania which resulted in the most concentrated wind damage occurring over Chautauqua County, while wind damage was more sporadic farther north across western New York. A storm survey was conducted in the following days near Lake Erie State Park in western Chautauqua County, but the damage observed was concluded to be caused by straight line winds.
episodes.181772: A warm front lifting northward through the area produced training showers and thunderstorms, which produced strong to severe damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall in East Tennessee.
episodes.181823: A strong monsoonal moisture push led to afternoon thunderstorms with heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding in Cheyenne and Laramie and areas in-between.
episodes.181981: A small cluster of thunderstorms produced a wind gust in Pender County, NC.
episodes.182058: A cold front moved through central Illinois during the day, interacting with an unstable airmass characterized by 3000 J/kg of CAPE. This resulted in scattered strong thunderstorms which produced isolated large hail.
episodes.182345: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours ahead of a cold front moving into the region.
episodes.182449: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized flooding in Pender County.
episodes.182484: There were numerous reports of hail and damaging wind gusts as a result of severe storms on July 20th.
episodes.182647: Isolated thunderstorms that featured frequent lightning struck a house, causing a house fire in Botetourt County.
episodes.182752: On the morning of July 20th, a warm front moved north through the forecast area, followed by a cold front in the late afternoon. Scattered supercells developed ahead of the cold front near the Indiana-Michigan Stateline. These thunderstorms dropped large hail in northern Indiana. As the storms organized and moved southeastward, they produced a widespread swath of wind damage (including numerous downed, uprooted, or snapped trees) in Fort Wayne, IN and into Van Wert, OH.
episodes.182753: On the morning of July 20th, a warm front moved north through the forecast area, followed by a cold front in the late afternoon. Scattered supercells developed ahead of the cold front near the Indiana-Michigan Stateline. These thunderstorms dropped large hail (up to 2.5 in diameter) between South Bend, IN and Elkhart, IN. As the storms organized and moved southeastward, they produced a widespread swath of wind damage (including numerous downed, uprooted, or snapped trees) in Fort Wayne, IN and into Van Wert, OH.
episodes.182780: In the morning of the 20th, widespread showers with some imbedded storm cells moved southeast through eastern Colorado. During the afternoon, a storm on the southern end of that same storm cluster intensified and caused extreme straight-line wind damage in West Central Kansas. A NWS Storm Survey team was sent out and determine maximum wind gusts to be 115 mph.  Some of the more significant damage included four sheds that were completely destroyed, two that were blown off their foundation, and two pieces of equipment that were pushed by the wind.  These storms also produced hail up to lime size.||Later in the evening another round of thunderstorms moved through West Central Kansas.   Wind gusts around 70 MPH were reported, along with some damage.
episodes.182826: A line of storms developed near a surface boundary in northern Nebraska in a deep shear environment and produced 1-inch hail in Knox County.
episodes.182925: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms dropped south-southeast during the early to mid afternoon hours into north central and northeast Alabama.  The tail end of this line spawned a couple of supercell thunderstorms which produced hail and even a brief funnel cloud. Also, damaging winds were reported resulting in power outages in Madison County.
episodes.183040: Thunderstorms moving through the Detroit and St. Clair Rivers produced wind gusts in excess of 40 knots. A waterspout was also reported over Lake St. Clair.
episodes.183041: Thunderstorms moving through southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts around 40 knots.
episodes.183100: A warm front moved across the Northland during the day on the 19th setting the stage for severe storms during the afternoon and evening across the region. The storms that developed were prolific hail producers with hail to the size of baseballs reported in northern Itasca County. A few isolated reported of tree damage were received, but hail was the primary threat from these storms. Additionally, lightning struck a barn that was over 100 years old starting a fire that completely destroyed the barn.
episodes.183129: A large squall-line (Mesoscale Convective System) moved across mainly North and East-Central GA during the afternoon and early evening hours of July 20th. Conditions were very favorable for damaging winds along and ahead of well-developed cold pool, with high instability and elevated Downdraft-CAPE. Widespread damage occurred from far north Georgia to east-central GA (Warren County), with very intense winds (80-90+mph) estimated from damage across parts of Cherokee and Forsyth counties. A couple of brief  embedded weak tornadoes occurred in Cherokee County from this system.
episodes.183359: The passage of a warm front during the morning of July 20th provided a moist and unstable air mass.  A strong, progressive upper trough tracked southeastward from the Great Lakes, with an associated cold front crossing during the evening hours. Mixed-layer CAPE of up to 2500 J/kg, strong deep shear, and steep low and mid-level lapse rates were supportive of severe weather.  Widespread reports of wind damage were received, mainly to trees.  Some isolated urban flash flooding also occurred in Beaver and Allegheny Counties.
episodes.183479: A shift in the atmospheric pattern from mid to late July brought an array of impacts to much of Utah, including severe thunderstorm wind gusts, large hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.183505: Scattered thunderstorms move west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm downed several trees on the Pascua Yaqui Pueblo.
episodes.183536: Severe storms moved into western Missouri during the morning of the 20th. A couple of these storms produced wind gusts over 60 mph, and localized flash flooding occurred over central Missouri as two to three inches of rain fell over areas that were saturated from the previous round of storms.
episodes.183560: On the evening of July 19th, showers and thunderstorms moved through the northwestern region of Kansas. Some of the thunderstorms became severe and produced hail up to quarters in size along with damaging wind gusts up to an estimated 90 mph.
episodes.183780: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts across portions of Adams, Denver, Elbert, Lincoln and Logan Counties.  The hail ranged in size from 1 to 2 inches in diameter.  Peak wind gusts up to around 70 mph were observed.  In Logan County, a spotter reported significant crop damage at their location.  The storms also caused tree damage as well as property damage to homes and vehicles.  In Elbert County, a greenhouse sustained damage and several chickens were killed.  In Lincoln County,  significant hail and wind damage was reported between Genoa and Arriba.   Several semi-trailers were flipped.  Several power poles also were also knocked down near the intersection of county roads 42 and 3P.  Heavy rain produced localized flash flooding in the Cameron Peak burn scar north of Glen Haven.
episodes.183793: Large hail and damaging winds were reported across western Kansas. Flooding was also reported across Garden City.
episodes.184178: Several supercell thunderstorms developed across the region and produce widespread hail, with occasional strong wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.184187: A line of strong storms formed over far eastern Wisconsin and moved over Lake Michigan during the morning, eventually tracking over nearshore waters off of Benzie county and producing estimated wind gusts in excess of 50 kts based on wind damage near the shoreline.
episodes.184188: A line of strong storms initiated along a cold front sliding across far eastern Wisconsin in the morning, eventually tracking over Lake Michigan into the forecast area. This line of storms produced severe wind gusts in the city of Frankfort, knocking down multiple trees and powerlines.
episodes.184266: Several sited measured 50 plus knot winds.
episodes.184325: Several supercell thunderstorms developed across the region and produce widespread hail, with occasional strong wind gusts and wind damage. Of particular note was hail that was 2 to 2.5 inches south of Rice Lake WI.
episodes.184383: A widespread area of strong to severe storms progressed through the Upper Mississippi River Valley during the nighttime hours of July 19th. As the storms reached counties in central Wisconsin, a general weakening trend resulted in decreasing intensity and spatial extent of storms. A damaging wind gust of 65 mph was recorded in western Clark County near the Town of Gilman.
episodes.184387: An upper level high pressure center was located over central Arizona and central New Mexico which resulted in a favorable pattern for efficient diurnal wind fluctuations including upslope oriented winds towards WFO Pueblo's eastern mountains. Weak waves embedded in the upper level northwesterly flow enhanced the lift and the pattern enhanced the deep shear. The result was a very rare mountainous tornado that was observed at around 9,000 feet.
episodes.184395: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough of low pressure produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.184452: A surface low moved generally eastward from east-central Lower MI to the southeastern shore of Lake Huron during the evening of the 20th. Simultaneously, the low's warm front swept northeastward across southern ON and western NY toward the northern shore of Lake Ontario as the low's trailing cold front moved generally eastward across southeastern Lower MI and far-northeastern IN to central Lake Erie and northeastern OH.||Multiple lines and clusters of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward and southeastward across northern OH during the early through mid-evening hours of the 20th and produced sporadic severe hail and straight-line convective wind damage as the storms encountered moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, within the warm sector. An embedded supercell produced large hail in Westlake, a western suburb of Cleveland. Although the thunderstorms moved progressively across the area, the thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall across Cuyahoga County, with instantaneous rainfall rates of 4 to 5 inches per hour and rainfall totals of 1.75 to 2.5 inches in a period of one hour or less. The torrential rainfall resulted in instances of flash flooding.
episodes.184469: As a cluster of storms moved east across southern Missouri into southern Illinois, some of the storms became severe with a few reports of damaging winds.
episodes.184470: As a cluster of storms moved east across southern Missouri into southern Illinois, some of the storms became severe with a few reports of damaging winds.
episodes.184874: Widespread strong to severe thunderstorms impacted the inland sounds, coastal waters, Pamlico, and Pungo Rivers bringing damaging winds during the evening hours on July 19th.
episodes.185596: A surface low moved east-southeastward from northwestern Lower MI to the southeastern shore of Lake Huron during the late morning through mid-evening of the 20th. Simultaneously, the low's warm front swept northeastward across northwestern PA to central Lake Ontario and central NY, and the low's trailing cold front moved generally eastward from northwestern Lower MI and southern Lake Michigan to southern Lake Huron and near the western shore of Lake Erie. Moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, were present just ahead of the surface warm front and within the warm sector.||A multicell thunderstorm in vicinity of the surface warm front persisted northeastward across northern portions of Erie County, including the city of Erie, during the early afternoon and produced severe hail and damaging convective wind gusts. A semi-discrete supercell then moved generally eastward across southern Erie County during the late afternoon through early evening and produced severe hail, including large hail of 2-inches in diameter in the Corry area. Following the supercell, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward and southeastward across northwest Pennsylvania and produced isolated straight-line convective wind damage in Conneautville, Crawford County.
episodes.185766: Lake Erie remained in the warm sector during the early to mid-evening of the 20th as a surface low moved from east-central Lower MI to southern Lake Huron and the trailing cold front moved east-southeastward across southeastern Lower MI toward the western shore of Lake Erie. Simultaneously, clusters and lines of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward and southeastward across much of Lake Erie. The storms generated strong to severe peak convective gusts along and near the northern OH shore as the storms encountered moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.

At approximately 6:18 pm MST, a witness saw a tree fall onto a 68-year-old bicyclist riding along the Denver and Rio Grande Western Rail paved multiuse trail. Law enforcement arrived on scene, finding the woman unconscious and pinned beneath the felled 40 to 50 ft tree. After being removed, life saving measures were preformed and she was transported to a local hospital in critical condition, where she later died from her injuries. The nearest observation in the area is from Hill AFB, which measured a gust of 67 mph at 6:26 pm MST. Other supporting wind gusts are noted from these strong storms in the area.

This particular tornado developed shortly after a large scale|straight line wind event unfolded across Pickens County. It should|be noted that while the tornado did considerable damage in the |span in which it was on the ground, the large scale straight line |wind damage across Pickens county southeastward was far more |considerable. The tornado formed on the north side a surge in the |winds along Long Swamp Church road very near the Bent Tree Lodge |and Vineyard and Angel on Horseback pavilion. Several trees were |snapped and uprooted in this area. The tornado continued eastward |through a wooded area crossing Dank road behind several homes on |the north side of Fitts Road. The tornado reached maximum |intensity as it crossed Fitts and Dank Roads where numerous trees |were snapped and uprooted, 1 home lost its roof, another home |sustained major roof damage and an outbuilding was destroyed. The |tornado continued southeast snapping and uprooting trees before |dissipating as it reached Skyline Drive. Peak winds were estimated around 95 mph (EF-1 tornado).

A survey of northern Cherokee County was done to assess whether|or not a tornado occurred.  The NWS assessment concluded that|widespread significant wind damage occurred and that a tornado|path within the large scale wind damage was not discernible.  The|particular area of focus started along Fincher Road east along|Dixon Road, crossing Upper Burris Road south to Land Road. |Significant tree damage and pockets of more significant tree|damage was noted in and around Dixon Road east to Upper Burris|Road.  Roof damage to homes in the area was also noted and used|to help estimate overall max wind speeds.  Tree fall patterns|along Dixon Road east across Upper Burris south to Land Road were|suggestive of a downburst in the region with a fanning out|pattern observed on on the ground. It should be noted that damage|was observed across an area over 3.5 miles wide.  Tree damage|extended north along Upper Bethany road over 1.5 miles north of|Land Road.  The survey concluded that maximum wind speeds within|the more significant pockets of damage likely reached 90 mph.

A survey of northern Forsyth County was done to assess whether or|not a tornado occurred. The NWS assessment concluded that|widespread significant wind damage occurred and that a tornado|path within the large scale wind damage was not discernible. The|particular area of focus started on Oak Grove Circle southeast|across Dahlonega Hwy, along Tallant Road and across Hopewell|Road. Radar data suggests that this region was located at the apex|of a bowing segment within the thunderstorm complex which had |already caused significant widespread wind damage. Tree fall |patterns along Tallant Road, Hopewell Rd and south of Tallant Road|along Dahlonega Hwy were more suggestive of straight line winds |or downburst due to the fanning out pattern observed. While it is |possible that a tornado can form along a leading edge of a bowing |segment which would resemble an eddy, we were unable to discern |from the damage if that had occurred. Regardless, a wind event |took place in this region which resembled mid range EF1 damage. |Several reporting stations throughout northern Forsyth County |recorded wind gusts of 68 and 69 mph. Winds with these pockets of |more intense tree damage, particularly along Tallant Road, is |estimated to have been 90-95mph.

The National Weather Service in Buffalo completed a storm survey|of damage from a line of thunderstorms which occurred during the|early evening of Thursday July 20, 2023. ||Storm damage surveyed was restricted to numerous, scattered |hardwood and softwood trees beginning in Lake Erie State Park near|Brocton, NY. Several trees were blown down, including a large pine|about 2 feet in diameter, and a large silver maple about 3 feet in|diameter. About a dozen large limbs were also blown down within |the park. The tree damage was sporadic, with most trees in the|park not showing any signs of damage. All of the trees and limbs |were blown down in a uniform direction, towards the east- |northeast in alignment with the track of the line of storms.||Widely scattered tree damage continued along Route 5 near the |Lake Erie shore from Lake Erie State Park to the south side of |Dunkirk, NY with several trees uprooted, and around a dozen large |tree limbs blown down. All of this tree damage was also aligned in|a uniform direction, towards the east-northeast.||All of the tree damage surveyed is consistent with straight line|thunderstorm wind damage, with peak wind gusts estimated near 75|mph based on the number and size of trees and limbs down.
